answer: One daily vote would require 10 fresh 512-token Falcon completions of disjoint nebula logs, assigned per key and day. Validators check key/day-bound proofs of a fixed inference kernel and single-use job IDs; missing or bad proofs deny the vote. n keys need 10n jobs: 5,120n output tokens. Inference consumes compute each day; GPUs are reusable capital. Honest allocation and sound proofs are essential: duplicate inputs let aliases reuse work despite new receipt IDs. Batching can cut costs, not job count; wealthy operators can still buy more votes.
